memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If you follow my decrees and are careful to obey my commands, I will
send you rain in its season, and the ground will yield its crops and the
trees their fruit'" - Lev 26:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here God begins to describe the blessings of obedience. Rain in its
season, fruitful ground, laden trees. To an agricultural people, this was
life itself.

We must read these promises carefully and in their proper place. This was
the specific covenant God made with the nation of Israel in the promised
land. Obedience and blessing, disobedience and hardship, were tied
together in that national covenant. It would be a mistake to lift these
verses out and turn them into a formula: obey God and you will always
prosper materially.

Scripture itself forbids that reading. Job was righteous and suffered.
Jesus was sinless and was crucified. Many of the most faithful believers
in history knew poverty, illness and loss. The prosperity gospel takes
verses like these and distorts them into a promise God never made to us.

Yet something true and unchanging shines here: God is the source of every
good thing. The rain, the harvest, the fruit — none of it comes from human
effort alone. James says every good and perfect gift is from above, coming
down from the Father (Jas 1:17).

The lasting principle is not "obey and get rich." It is that walking with
God is the path of true life, and that all genuine provision flows from
His hand. Under the New Covenant, our deepest blessings are spiritual —
every spiritual blessing in Christ (Eph 1:3).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I tempted to treat God as a means to material reward?
2. Do I recognise God as the source behind every good thing I have?
3. What spiritual blessings in Christ have I been overlooking?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You are the source of every good gift. Guard me from treating You
as a way to get things, and help me treasure the blessings I have in
Christ above all. Amen.
